sections.h2: Where do Nicholas County property owners go with tax questions?
sections.html:
Both offices are in the Nicholas County Courthouse at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle. The PVA sits in the basement and answers valuation questions at 859-289-3735, Monday through Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. The Sheriff's Office, at 859-289-3740, collects the tax.

The PVA's mailing address is P.O. Box 2, Carlisle, KY 40311. The PVA website carries the certified tax roll, a tax estimator, forms and a fee schedule, and it explains that the office exists to help owners understand how assessments are made.

The county sheriff's own page describes the job as collecting taxes along with public safety. Because the sheriff only collects, a dispute over a figure on the bill starts at the PVA, not at the sheriff's desk.

Nicholas County is one of Kentucky's smallest and most rural counties. Carlisle is the county seat and the only incorporated community, and the Census Bureau's 2020 count classes all residents as rural. The county was formed in 1799 from Bourbon and Mason counties and has 195 square miles of land, with farms, wooded hollows and small villages typical of the Bluegrass belt.

History runs through it. Forest Retreat, a district on the National Register of Historic Places, was built in 1814, and the cabin Daniel Boone built in 1795 is marked on U.S. 68. Blue Licks Battlefield State Resort Park, which covers 148 acres near Mount Olivet, lies partly in Nicholas County and commemorates an August 1782 battle.

Commuting shapes the market. The Census Bureau puts the mean trip to work at 35.6 minutes, longer than in Montgomery, Muhlenberg or Nelson County, and a sign that many residents work outside Nicholas County. Total employment inside the county was only 415 in 2023, across 82 employer establishments, so most buyers are not tied to a local employer.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Nicholas County housing?
sections.html:
With 7,949 people estimated for July 2025, up 5.5% from the 2020 base, Nicholas County is small enough that a handful of sales can move the averages. QuickFacts lists these housing figures.

  • Housing units, 2025 estimate: 3,355. Building permits in 2025: 3.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 74.5%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $123,000.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,143 with a mortgage and $426 without.
  • Median gross rent: $728.
  • Median household income: $59,531, and 16.2% of residents live in poverty.

Only 9.8% of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree, and 10.3% of people under 65 lack health insurance. Roughly 92.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the steadiest figure of the four counties on this list.

sections.h2: When are Nicholas County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The PVA's site announced that the 2026 bills would be mailed on or about October 1, 2026. The payment steps follow KRS 134.015.

Nicholas County payment schedule under KRS 134.015
When paidWhat applies
By November 12% off the bill
November 2 through December 31Amount on the bill
January 1 through January 315% penalty
After January 3110% penalty

The statute stops at 10%, while the Montgomery, Muhlenberg and Nelson County sheriffs each post a 21% penalty for February 1 to April 15. Ask the Nicholas County Sheriff at 859-289-3740 for the figure that applies on the day you plan to pay.

sections.h2: What does a late Nicholas County bill cost?
sections.html:
A $800 bill costs $784 with the discount and $800 at face value. In January it is $840. If a 21% penalty applies from February, as other Kentucky sheriffs post, it is $968.

The 10% statutory penalty is measured on taxes due and unpaid. The statute also calls the tax, fees, penalties and interest a personal debt of the taxpayer from the assessment date until paid.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Nicholas County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference with the Nicholas County PVA or a deputy. KRS 133.120 makes that conference the first step, and it must happen before or during the inspection period or during any extension the state grants. The PVA must explain the constitutional and statutory rules and how your value was derived, and the office keeps a record of what was discussed.

The inspection period opens the first Monday in May and runs 13 days under KRS 133.045. If the conference does not settle it, send the County Clerk a letter or petition that identifies the parcel, gives your reasons and states your opinion of fair cash value. The deadline is one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals then holds a hearing, where you may make an audio recording of the proceedings.

A filed appeal never postpones payment. You pay on the value you stated, and the final value decides what else is owed, with interest.

sections.h2: Can Nicholas County seniors or disabled owners get a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, can claim the statewide exemption. The Department of Revenue sets it at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. A home assessed at the county median of $123,000 would be taxed on $73,900.

The application goes to the Nicholas County PVA in the courthouse basement. Disability claims must be renewed every year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or is permanently and totally disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

sections.h2: Who gets the tax bill after a Nicholas County sale?
sections.html:
The Nicholas County PVA explains that Kentucky assesses all property as of January 1, and that ownership for tax purposes is also fixed on that date. If a house is bought after January 1, state statute requires the bill to be issued in the former owner's name until the next calendar year. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the new owner using information from a tax agreement signed by buyer or seller. A buyer who receives nothing can get a copy from the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

  • Seller: confirm the current bill is paid and keep the receipt.
  • Buyer: provide a mailing address on the deed's in-care-of line, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • Both sides: decide in the contract how the year's tax is prorated.
  • Estate sales: the personal representative files an affidavit with the County Clerk listing recipients and values before closing out the estate.

faqs.q: Where is the Nicholas County PVA office?
faqs.a: It is in the basement of the courthouse at 125 East Main Street in Carlisle, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. The phone is 859-289-3735.

faqs.q: Who sends a tax bill to a new owner in Nicholas County?
faqs.a: The bill is issued in the former owner's name until the next calendar year, and the PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer. A buyer who gets none can call the sheriff at 859-289-3740.

faqs.q: How much is the discount for paying Nicholas County tax early?
faqs.a: It is 2% of the bill when paid in full by November 1. From November 2 through December 31 the plain amount is due.

faqs.q: How much is the penalty in Nicholas County after January?
faqs.a: KRS 134.015 sets a 5% penalty for January and 10% after January 31. Sheriff collection fees can raise the total, so ask the sheriff for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky homestead exemption for Nicholas County owners?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years and applies to owners 65 or older or totally disabled. File with the Nicholas County PVA.
